pr.body:
closes #37118

PR is adding some context information to be available in the `access-token` without a need to introduce any additional custom claims. So far, it provides info about:

- session type (online, offline, transient), which was used to create the token
- token type (regular or lightweight token)
- grant type

These informations can be useful when token is later sent to some Keycloak endpoints (for example introspection, userInfo, admin/account REST API) to optimize something. For example:
- session-type will allow to lookup only correct session type based on the type of the session, which token was created from. As for example today, we need to lookup "online" session and if it is not found, then fallback to "offline" session. So possible unnecessary lookup. Related follow-up issue for optimize that: #37662

- Grant type knowledge can be useful for example for the token-exchange use-case: #37117

- Lightweight access token: We will be able to recognize more reliably if access-token is lightweight or not and do something based on that (EG. lookup roles from model instead of lookup roles from the token)

In this PR, I've made token ID to look something like `onrtac:1f65761e-1c69-40a2-82da-2d8aa5e39a8a` .
  - The first 2 characters is shortcut for "session type" - `on` is shortcut for "online" session
  - The next 2 characters is shortcut for "token type" - `rt` is shortcut for regular token (not lightweight token)
  - The next 2 characters is shortcut for grant type - `ac` is shortcut for "authorization code" grant

Shortcuts are used, so the token ID contains important info, but at the same time, it is limited in size and does not introduce much new characters to the token.

The encoding into ID is used only for access-tokens. Not used for refresh tokens or ID tokens or any others.

Introduced dedicated SPI in the end. Wanted to "cache" some objects (EG. shortcuts for grant types etc) and it seems clearer to me to cache them at the level of factory, rather than in the static fields, which is not very pretty. Moreover, provider adds ability for someone to introduce his own provider (and eventually encode some more info or encode stuff in the different way etc).

#### Note

I've used 2 commits in this PR. Originally, in the 1st commit, I've made the encoding a bit longer with token ID to look something like `st.on_tt.rt_gt.ac:1f65761e-1c69-40a2-82da-2d8aa5e39a8a` .
  - The `st` is shortcut for "session type" and `on` is shortcut for "online" session
  - The `tt` is shortcut for "token type" and `rt` is shortcut for regular token (not lightweight token)
  - The `gt` is shortcut for grant type and `ac` is shortcut for "authorization code" grant

But assuming that every "type" has always 2 characters long shortcut, I've rather updated it in the 2nd commit to have only 7 new characters instead of 18 characters. I planned to squash before merge (unless you think that we should rather use longer format for some reason, in which case the 2nd commit can be removed from the PR).
pr.title: Encoding context to access token IDs

raw_findings.body: A null rawTokenId silently passes construction; encodeTokenId then concatenates it as the literal string "null" (e.g. "onrtac:null"), producing a corrupt token ID instead of failing fast with the intended NullPointerException message.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Constructor invariant for rawTokenId is never enforced, allowing invalid state to propagate into encoded token IDs.
raw_findings.impact: A null rawTokenId silently passes construction; encodeTokenId then concatenates it as the literal string "null" (e.g. "onrtac:null"), producing a corrupt token ID instead of failing fast with the intended NullPointerException message.
raw_findings.root_cause: Copy-paste error: the requireNonNull intended for rawTokenId re-checks grantType while carrying the rawTokenId message.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Change the second duplicated check to Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");
raw_findings.title: Duplicated null-check validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
raw_findings.trigger: Constructing an AccessTokenContext with a null rawTokenId (e.g. a custom TokenContextEncoderProvider or caller passing null as the generated ID).

raw_findings.body: The matcher returns false when the shortcut equals the expectation and true when it differs, so tokens encoded with the wrong grant type pass the assertion (and a correctly encoded token would fail it), removing the regression coverage this matcher was added to provide.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test assertion accepts incorrect grant-type encodings, so regressions in token ID encoding go undetected.
raw_findings.impact: The matcher returns false when the shortcut equals the expectation and true when it differs, so tokens encoded with the wrong grant type pass the assertion (and a correctly encoded token would fail it), removing the regression coverage this matcher was added to provide.
raw_findings.root_cause: Missing '!' negation in the equality guard of the new TypeSafeMatcher.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Negate the comparison: if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;
raw_findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher condition is inverted, making the grant-shortcut assertion vacuous
raw_findings.trigger: Any test using expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken; a token ID whose grant shortcut does NOT match the expected shortcut still satisfies the matcher.

raw_findings.body: substring(3, 5) spans the last tokenType character and the first grantType character (e.g. 'ta' from 'onrtac'), so the comparison never inspects the actual grant shortcut; even after fixing the inverted condition the matcher would reject all correctly encoded token IDs.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Matcher compares the wrong two characters, so the grant-shortcut assertion can never validate the encoded grant type.
raw_findings.impact: substring(3, 5) spans the last tokenType character and the first grantType character (e.g. 'ta' from 'onrtac'), so the comparison never inspects the actual grant shortcut; even after fixing the inverted condition the matcher would reject all correctly encoded token IDs.
raw_findings.root_cause: Off-by-one indexing that contradicts the encoding layout documented in the adjacent comment ("starts at character 4th char").
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use items[0].substring(4, 6) to align with the encoder layout and the matcher's own comment.
raw_findings.title: isAccessTokenId extracts grant shortcut with wrong substring indices (3,5) instead of (4,6)
raw_findings.trigger: Any token ID produced by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider, whose 6-char prefix places the grant shortcut at indices 4-5 (per the encoder: sessionType chars 0-1, tokenType chars 2-3, grantType chars 4-5).

raw_findings.body: Access tokens issued through the client_credentials grant encode the UNKNOWN shortcut "na" in the token ID instead of "cc", defeating the PR's goal of reliably deriving grant type from the token and misleading downstream consumers (introspection, token-exchange optimizations).
raw_findings.failure_mode: Token IDs for client_credentials tokens carry an incorrect 'unknown' grant marker despite a shortcut being registered for the grant.
raw_findings.impact: Access tokens issued through the client_credentials grant encode the UNKNOWN shortcut "na" in the token ID instead of "cc", defeating the PR's goal of reliably deriving grant type from the token and misleading downstream consumers (introspection, token-exchange optimizations).
raw_findings.root_cause: The GRANT_TYPE attribute propagation was added only to OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse and a few individual grants, missing grants that build the token response themselves.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Set clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType()) in ClientCredentialsGrantType.process() before generateAccessToken(), or set the attribute centrally in OAuth2GrantTypeBase.setContext/process so every grant is covered.
raw_findings.title: Client credentials grant never sets GRANT_TYPE attribute, so its 'cc' shortcut is never encoded
raw_findings.trigger: A client_credentials token request: ClientCredentialsGrantType builds the response via tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken() directly (ClientCredentialsGrantType.java L140-141) and never calls createTokenResponse, which is the only base-class path that sets clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, ...).

raw_findings.body: Access tokens issued through the UMA grant encode the UNKNOWN shortcut "na" instead of "pg", so the registered shortcut is dead code and downstream consumers cannot distinguish UMA-issued tokens as intended by this PR.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Token IDs for UMA tokens carry an incorrect 'unknown' grant marker despite a shortcut being registered for the grant.
raw_findings.impact: Access tokens issued through the UMA grant encode the UNKNOWN shortcut "na" instead of "pg", so the registered shortcut is dead code and downstream consumers cannot distinguish UMA-issued tokens as intended by this PR.
raw_findings.root_cause: GRANT_TYPE attribute propagation was not added to the UMA/AuthorizationTokenService token creation path even though a shortcut was defined for the grant.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Set the Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute on the ClientSessionContext in the UMA token issuance path (PermissionGrantType/AuthorizationTokenService) before the access token is generated.
raw_findings.title: UMA permission grant never sets GRANT_TYPE attribute, so its 'pg' shortcut is never encoded
raw_findings.trigger: A UMA token request (grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:uma-ticket): the token is created via AuthorizationTokenService's responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken() (AuthorizationTokenService.java L358), which never sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE on the clientSessionCtx.

raw_findings.suggested_fix: Catch IllegalArgumentException specifically (matching the sibling testOldToken which catches IllegalStateException), or use Assert.assertThrows(IllegalArgumentException.class, ...).

validated_findings.trigger: A client_credentials token request: ClientCredentialsGrantType builds the response via tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken() directly (ClientCredentialsGrantType.java L140-141) and never calls createTokenResponse, which is the only base-class path that sets clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, ...).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that ClientCredentialsGrantType never sets GRANT_TYPE is speculative. The patch shows OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse sets the attribute at line 109, but ClientCredentialsGrantType uses responseBuilder directly. However, without seeing the full token generation path and whether the attribute is read elsewhere, this is ungrounded speculation about runtime behavior.

validated_findings.body: Access tokens issued through the UMA grant encode the UNKNOWN shortcut "na" instead of "pg", so the registered shortcut is dead code and downstream consumers cannot distinguish UMA-issued tokens as intended by this PR.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Token IDs for UMA tokens carry an incorrect 'unknown' grant marker despite a shortcut being registered for the grant.
validated_findings.impact: Access tokens issued through the UMA grant encode the UNKNOWN shortcut "na" instead of "pg", so the registered shortcut is dead code and downstream consumers cannot distinguish UMA-issued tokens as intended by this PR.
validated_findings.root_cause: GRANT_TYPE attribute propagation was not added to the UMA/AuthorizationTokenService token creation path even though a shortcut was defined for the grant.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Set the Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute on the ClientSessionContext in the UMA token issuance path (PermissionGrantType/AuthorizationTokenService) before the access token is generated.
validated_findings.title: UMA permission grant never sets GRANT_TYPE attribute, so its 'pg' shortcut is never encoded
validated_findings.trigger: A UMA token request (grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:uma-ticket): the token is created via AuthorizationTokenService's responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken() (AuthorizationTokenService.java L358), which never sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE on the clientSessionCtx.
